consumer_step: 1.1 The map $u\mapsto(u,0)$ is continuous and hence Borel measurable; [F4] makes the formula in the statement its pushforward measure, and [A2, F3] give its total mass $\lambda_1([0,1])=1$. It assigns mass one to the Borel segment $L$. For each integer $n\ge1$, the segment lies in the rectangle $[0,1]\times[-1/n,1/n]$, whose Lebesgue area is $2/n$ by [F3]. Therefore its outer measure is at most $2/n$ for every $n$, hence its Lebesgue measure is zero. Since $\mu(L)=1$ and Lebesgue measure of $L$ is zero, $\mu$ is singular with respect to two-dimensional Lebesgue measure. [A2, F3, F4, given, algebra]
